harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Restored branch_orders on node1 with exact keys, relationships, and monetary values. Configured persistent read-only reporting access from node2 and retained DBA write access. Both nodes passed serial reboot and recovery verification without changing CentOS or the kernel.
actions_performed: Restored the supplied SQL export without modifying it.
Enabled MySQL at boot and restricted TCP/3306 access to node2.
Created branch_report with SELECT-only access and branch_dba with full database privileges.
Stored protected client profiles on node2 and node1 respectively.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Restore relational data with supplied primary keys, customer/order relationships, and exact monetary values
evidence.summary: Schema proves the primary and foreign keys plus DECIMAL(10,2); queries return IDs 10/20 and 101/102/103 with values 12.35, 99.90, and 0.05.

evidence.requirement: Reporting account can read from node2 but cannot change data
evidence.summary: node2 authenticated as branch_report@10.100.73.11, read both tables, and received ERROR 1142 on UPDATE before and after restarts.
branch_dba has ALL privileges on branch_orders and successfully executed a rolled-back insert probe.
orders.sql remains 452 bytes with unchanged MD5 89fb2d832262f01caae30a937c43169a.

evidence.requirement: Retain the legacy OS release and kernel with compatible software
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5; node1 runs CentOS-compatible MySQL 5.0.95.
Healthy baseline and old boot ID were captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed, and MySQL, data, export, listener, and node2 reporting access recovered.
Healthy remote-data baseline and old boot ID were captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed, and the protected reporting profile, reads, exact data, and write denial recovered.
